l4_steps.name: Subscribe to FAA rulemaking & ICAO SARPs updates
l4_steps.input: FAA NPRM publications, ICAO amendment cycles, DOT safety directives
l4_steps.output: Regulatory watch list with effective dates and applicability flags
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of applicable NPRMs captured within 5 business days of publication
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA issues 300+ NPRMs per year; manual triage against 14 CFR Part 119/121 scope causes missed applicability deadlines without automated rule-matching

l4_steps.name: Classify regulatory change by AOC impact category
l4_steps.input: Regulatory watch list, current Operations Specifications (OpSpecs) baseline
l4_steps.output: Impact classification: Critical / Significant / Administrative; assigned owner and deadline
l4_steps.kpi: Classification completed within 3 business days of receipt; ≥95% accuracy validated by VP Safety review
l4_steps.pain_point: 14 CFR Part 121 overlaps with Part 91, Part 135, and ICAO Annex 6 — misclassification risk is high for carriers operating international routes under bilateral agreements

l4_steps.name: Determine material impact on AOC or OpSpecs conditions
l4_steps.input: Impact classification, current OpSpecs (OpSpec A, B, C, D series)
l4_steps.output: Go/no-go decision: initiate gap assessment or log as no-action required
l4_steps.kpi: Decision documented within 2 business days; 0 unreviewed critical items older than 5 days
l4_steps.pain_point: OpSpecs are issued at aircraft-type level — a single Boeing 737 MAX amendment may trigger parallel OpSpec revisions across A002, B036, and D085 series, each requiring separate FAA FSDO concurrence

l4_steps.name: Conduct OpSpecs gap analysis against new regulation
l4_steps.input: Applicable regulatory change, current approved OpSpecs, Operations Manual
l4_steps.output: Gap analysis report with non-compliant clauses, affected flight types, and remediation scope
l4_steps.kpi: Gap analysis completed ≥30 days before regulation effective date for non-emergency rules
l4_steps.pain_point: WebOPSS does not provide automated diff between existing OpSpecs and new regulatory text — analysts must perform manual line-by-line comparison across 100+ OpSpec paragraphs, consuming 40+ analyst-hours per major rule change

l4_steps.name: Review fleet type ratings and pilot training compliance
l4_steps.input: Gap analysis report, approved Training Specifications (TRSpecs), FAR Part 121 Subpart N/O
l4_steps.output: Training compliance matrix: current vs. required qualification levels by aircraft type and route
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of pilots current on type rating within 24-month recurrent cycle; 0 flights dispatched with lapsed qualification
l4_steps.pain_point: Introduction of new flight deck technology (e.g., Boeing 737 MAX MCAS differences training) requires FSDO-approved training programme amendments before revenue flying — timeline mismatch with aircraft delivery schedules creates capacity risk

l4_steps.name: Identify non-compliance gaps and remediation requirements
l4_steps.input: Gap analysis report, training compliance matrix, airworthiness directives (ADs) list
l4_steps.output: Non-compliance register with risk severity rating (Critical / High / Medium / Low)
l4_steps.kpi: Zero Critical-rated gaps open beyond 30 days; High-rated gaps resolved within 90 days
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA Airworthiness Directives issued via AD registry may conflict with manufacturer service bulletin schedules — carriers must negotiate alternate means of compliance (AMOC) approval which averages 6–18 months with FAA Aircraft Certification Office

l4_steps.name: Develop and approve corrective action plan (CAP)
l4_steps.input: Non-compliance register, resource constraints, budget from SAP S/4HANA Finance
l4_steps.output: Board-approved CAP with milestones, accountable owners, and target closure dates
l4_steps.kpi: CAP approved by VP Safety within 10 business days of gap identification; milestone adherence ≥90%
l4_steps.pain_point: CAP funding competes with capital allocation cycles — safety-driven OpEx spend cannot be deferred but lacks the revenue justification framework used for commercial projects, creating budget approval delays

l4_steps.name: Prepare AOC amendment or OpSpecs revision package
l4_steps.input: Approved CAP, draft revised OpSpecs, supporting technical documentation
l4_steps.output: Complete FAA amendment package: Form 8900-1, revised OpSpec paragraphs, supporting data
l4_steps.kpi: Package completeness score ≥95% on first submission (measured by FAA deficiency rate); zero incomplete submissions
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA Form 8900-1 and WebOPSS data entry does not validate cross-references between OpSpec series — errors discovered during FSDO review require full resubmission and add 4–8 weeks to approval timeline

l4_steps.name: Submit amendment package to FAA FSDO via WebOPSS
l4_steps.input: Completed amendment package, principal operations inspector (POI) contact
l4_steps.output: FAA submission confirmation number; amendment tracking record opened in ARMS
l4_steps.kpi: Submission made ≥60 days before effective date for Major amendments; ≥30 days for Minor
l4_steps.pain_point: WebOPSS portal has documented uptime issues during peak submission periods (e.g., end-of-year deadline rush); carriers with sole-source FSDO assignment have no alternative submission channel if POI is on extended leave

l4_steps.name: Respond to FAA requests for additional information
l4_steps.input: FAA deficiency notice or Request for Additional Information (RAI)
l4_steps.output: Supplemental data package; revised submission if OpSpec text changes required
l4_steps.kpi: RAI response submitted within 10 business days of receipt; first-response resolution rate ≥75%
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA POI reviewer rotation means institutional knowledge of airline-specific OpSpecs is lost — new POI may re-open previously resolved items, causing amendment cycles to restart and exceeding planned compliance timelines

l4_steps.name: Receive, validate, and file approved OpSpecs revision
l4_steps.output: Updated OpSpecs filed in controlled document repository; affected departments notified
l4_steps.kpi: Distribution to operational departments within 24 hours of FAA approval; acknowledgement receipt rate 100% within 48 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: OpSpecs revisions must be cascaded to Dispatch, Crew Training, Maintenance, and Ground Ops simultaneously — document management systems (SharePoint) lack mandatory-read workflow enforcement, creating compliance traceability gaps

l4_steps.name: Conduct periodic SMS internal compliance audit
l4_steps.input: Annual audit schedule, ICAO Doc 9859 SMS framework, 14 CFR §119.65 requirements
l4_steps.output: Internal audit report with findings, risk ratings, and corrective action recommendations
l4_steps.kpi: 4 SMS audits completed per year; critical findings closed within 30 days; audit coverage ≥100% of SMS components annually
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA requires SMS programmes to demonstrate safety performance improvement over time (AC 120-92B) — carriers using spreadsheet-based audit tracking cannot produce trend evidence required for IOSA (IATA Operational Safety Audit) recertification

l4_steps.name: Analyse FOQA safety performance indicators against thresholds
l4_steps.input: Flight recorder data feeds, airline-defined safety performance indicator (SPI) thresholds
l4_steps.output: SPI dashboard report: exceedance counts, trend analysis, risk-ranked event list
l4_steps.kpi: FOQA data capture rate ≥99.5% of revenue flights; SPI exceedance rate <0.5 per 1,000 flights for high-severity events
l4_steps.pain_point: FOQA data volumes from 800+ daily flights generate 2TB+ per month — without automated anomaly detection (e.g., Palantir Aviation Safety), manual analyst review creates a 4–6 week lag between exceedance event and corrective action initiation

l4_steps.name: File ASAP or VDRP voluntary safety disclosure report
l4_steps.role: Pilot / Dispatcher / Aviation Safety Action Program (ASAP) Manager
l4_steps.system: FAA Aviation Safety Action Program (ASAP) Portal
l4_steps.input: SPI threshold breach, pilot self-disclosure, or near-miss event report
l4_steps.output: ASAP Event Review Committee (ERC) report; corrective action recommendation to FAA
l4_steps.kpi: ASAP report submission within 24 hours of event identification; ERC review completed within 30 days; 0 reports rejected for lateness
l4_steps.pain_point: ASAP programme confidentiality protections (14 CFR §13.401) conflict with labour contract grievance procedures — ambiguity over which events qualify for ASAP immunity vs. disciplinary action suppresses voluntary disclosure rates, undermining SMS effectiveness

l4_steps.name: Update MEL, Operations Manual, and training materials
l4_steps.input: Approved OpSpecs revision, AD compliance status, ASAP corrective actions
l4_steps.output: Revised MEL amendments, updated Operations Manual sections, EFB content pushed to fleet tablets
l4_steps.kpi: MEL and Ops Manual updates published within 5 business days of OpSpecs approval; EFB content sync to 100% of fleet devices within 24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: MEL amendment cycle requires simultaneous approval from airline, Boeing (MMEL source), and FAA — three-party review adds 60–120 days per amendment, creating temporary deferred maintenance item backlogs that inflate maintenance cost and aircraft availability risk

l4_steps.name: Track and report compliance costs against regulatory budget
l4_steps.input: CAP milestones, training programme costs, audit fees, legal advisory costs
l4_steps.output: Regulatory compliance cost report by OpSpec category; variance analysis vs. annual budget
l4_steps.kpi: Regulatory compliance budget variance ≤5% quarterly; cost-per-amendment tracked and benchmarked annually
l4_steps.pain_point: Regulatory compliance costs are scattered across Safety, Legal, Crew Training, and Maintenance cost centres in SAP — absence of a dedicated regulatory compliance WBS element prevents accurate total-cost-of-compliance reporting required by board audit committees

l4_steps.name: Archive compliance records and close regulatory cycle
l4_steps.input: Approved OpSpecs, audit reports, ASAP ERC decisions, CAP closure evidence
l4_steps.output: Compliance cycle closure report; archived records indexed for 7-year retention per 14 CFR §121.380
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of compliance records archived within 5 business days of cycle close; retrieval time for auditor requests ≤1 business day
l4_steps.pain_point: 14 CFR §121.380 mandates 7-year retention for most compliance records, but GDPR and state privacy laws impose conflicting deletion requirements for records containing crew personal data — dual-obligation conflict requires manual legal review for each retention decision
